Thanks for the heads-up, Ellen — appreciate the transparency. Short summary of where we are internally and a concrete proposal below.

Context (internal): we have the MAP committed to the June 15 close with milestone gating for integration, acceptance tests, and final payment. Procurement delays are a common close slippage trigger; we usually handle in one of three ways:
- Freeze pricing for a defined extension window (7–21 days) without further commercial rework.
- Offer a small, time-bound credit to cover incremental runway risk.
- Rebaseline the MAP to shift non-critical acceptance items into a phased post-close workstream while keeping a limited acceptance gate for the initial go-live.

Proposal for Medi aCorp (fast path):
1) Redwood will hold pricing and the MAP commitments for a 14-day extension (to 2027-06-29) provided procurement confirms the updated audit timeline by EOD 2027-06-07.
2) If procurement sign-off slips beyond 2027-06-29, Redwood will offer a one-time operational credit of 5% of first-year committed usage, capped at $25k, in lieu of re-negotiating pricing.
3) As contingency, we propose a phased acceptance approach: core API and internal routing validated pre-signature and secondary analytics/longer-term optimizations scheduled into a 30-day post-close window.

I have drafted a rebaseline MAP and a risk log — attaching both. Can @Karthik and @Laura confirm feasibility on the phased acceptance approach (Karthik: runtime/integration; Laura: commercial/credit approval)? Jonas, flagging if you want to loop in execs for signoff above the $25k cap.

Attached: MAP_v3.xlsx, close_risk_log.csv, proposed-credit-term.pdf

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Priyom / team — quick technical read: phased acceptance is workable with two constraints:
1) We need the customer to commit to the initial integration milestones (API keys, network allowlist, sample workload) before we provision dedicated capacity for the first wave. That can be completed independently of full procurement sign-off if procurement agrees in writing to proceed with initial tech validation.
2) Any go-live that requires Dedicated pools (reserved GPUs) must be scheduled for after purchase order issuance. We can run a limited hosted trial to validate performance prior to PO.

If Medi aCorp is comfortable with an "integration-first / purchase-order-later" path for initial validation, I'm fine with the 14-day hold and the 30-day follow-on window. We'll need to add a checklist to the MAP for the integration gate to avoid surprises.

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Agree with the staged approach. A couple of commercial notes:
- I can approve up to $15k in one-time operational credit against year-one fees. Anything >$15k requires approval from Jonas / Revenue Ops per our delegation matrix.
- If we hold pricing for an extension, we should capture a written commitment from the customer to a revised MAP timeline and a PO target date; otherwise the hold becomes open-ended risk.

If we offer the 5% / $25k cap you suggested, and we want to avoid exec escalation, I'd propose we tweak to a firm 5% credit capped at $15k and require the customer to sign the MAP_v3 (rebaseline) within 3 business days of our proposal. If they sign, we lock pricing for 14 days.

I'll draft the short amendment language for the MAP once we decide the cap.

—Laura

Thanks team. I'm ok with Laura's adjusted cap ($15k) to keep moving without exec attention. Two asks:
1) Make the offer conditional on Medi aCorp signing the revised MAP (MAP_v3) within 72 hours of receipt. Capture the revised PO target date in the amendment.
2) Add an explicit fall-back: if PO is not received within 30 days of the signed MAP, we reserve the right to revisit list pricing (we should call this out in the amendment).

If that's acceptable, Priyom please send a short, customer-facing note that includes the revised MAP, the credit amount, and the acceptance/PO deadlines. I'll review prior to sending to the executive buyer if anything >$15k becomes necessary.

-Jonas

Ellen — thanks again for the update and for working with us on a pragmatic path. Per our internal alignment, here's the formal proposal to keep the project on track without reopening pricing: 

1) 14-day extension: Redwood will hold current pricing and commitments for a 14-day extension (new target close: 2027-06-29) provided Medi aCorp confirms the updated procurement audit timeline by 2027-06-07.

2) Limited operational credit: Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 5% of the first-year committed usage, capped at $15,000, contingent upon Medi aCorp signing the enclosed MAP_v3 by 2027-06-11 (72 hours from proposal delivery).

3) Phased acceptance path: core integration and API validation can proceed prior to PO issuance as long as procurement provides a written acknowledgement to proceed with initial technical validation. Dedicated capacity go-live remains contingent on PO.

4) Fallback clause: if a PO is not received within 30 days of the signed MAP, Redwood reserves the right to revisit pricing and contract terms.

Next steps (requested):
- Ellen / procurement: confirm the audit timeline and whether procurement can provide a written acknowledgement for initial tech validation by 2027-06-07.
- Medi aCorp: sign MAP_v3 (attached) by 2027-06-11 to secure the credit and 14-day pricing hold.

We hope this balances commercial certainty for both sides and keeps the project moving. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the phased checklist.

Best,
Priyom Das
